name: Invisalign attachments / chewies

card.summary: Small bonded bumps and rubbery bite cylinders that help clear aligners grip and seat; useful accessories with little dedicated research.
card.note: Attachments are placed by a clinician; chewies are an adjunct, and aligners overall have limits for some movements.

quick.overview:
Clear aligners are plastic trays that move teeth in stages. Two accessories come up constantly: attachments, which are small tooth-colored composite shapes bonded to teeth, and chewies, soft cylinders users bite on to press the tray fully onto the teeth.

Attachments are part of the treatment plan set by the clinician. Chewies are mostly discussed by patients as a way to help trays seat; sources reviewed give no dedicated trial of them.
quick.mechanism: Because plastic is less rigid than metal, attachments give the tray something to push against so it can rotate or pull down teeth. Chewies work by biting force pressing the tray against the teeth to close small gaps.
quick.risks: More attachments can make the aligners look less discreet. Aligners in general are considered less effective than braces for rotations, extrusion and front-to-back jaw discrepancies, and relapse is reported.

lead: Attachments are small tooth-colored composite shapes bonded to certain teeth during clear aligner treatment. They help the aligner rotate or pull down teeth, since the plastic is less rigid than metal [1]. Chewies are soft cylinders that wearers bite on to help seat an aligner; they are an informal accessory and are not covered in the encyclopedic sources reviewed.

Clear aligners typically move teeth about 0.25 to 0.33 mm per stage, are worn around 22 hours a day, and treatment averages about 13.5 months [1]. A 2014 systematic review found study quality insufficient to determine effectiveness, and aligners are considered less effective than conventional braces for rotations, extrusion and jaw discrepancies [1].
infobox: Soft bite cylinders for seating trays

paras: Attachments are bonded by a clinician to selected teeth. More attachments can make aligners less aesthetically pleasing [1]. Chewies are used by the wearer at home and are commonly discussed on patient forums.

Align Technology, maker of Invisalign, was founded in 1997 by Zia Chishti, with US sales beginning in 1999. Orthodontists were initially resistant, but consumers embraced the product, and 80,000 dentists had been trained by 2014 [1].

Aligners are likely useful for moderate front-teeth crowding but less effective than braces for rotations, extrusion and front-back jaw discrepancies, and relapse of front teeth has been reported more often. They are not recommended for children [1]. A nightly retainer is usually advised after treatment [1].
No studies found on chewies specifically. Studies of clear aligners as a category are described as of insufficient quality to establish effectiveness [1].

timeline.event: Align Technology founded by Zia Chishti [1].
